# Chichén Itzá Walk

> Independent visitor guide to Chichén Itzá, Yucatán, Mexico. Practical, up-to-date (2026) advice on tickets and the single Boleto Único entry fee, opening hours, the relocated entrance, the best time to go, self-guided walking routes, day trips from Cancún, Tulum, Playa del Carmen and Mérida, and what each monument means — plus a self-guided offline audio walk by TouringBee. Available in 8 languages: English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Polish and Russian.

This site is a TouringBee project. It is independent and not affiliated with INAH, the government of Yucatán or the administration of the Chichén Itzá archaeological zone. Some links are affiliate links (Tiqets, GetYourGuide, Booking.com, TouringBee); they never affect what is recommended.

## Key facts (2026)

- Entry for foreign adults: about 697 MXN total (~€35 / $40) — one ticket at one window since the Boleto Único replaced the two-counter system in spring 2026; the 105 MXN federal INAH fee is bundled in. Mexican nationals about 310 MXN, Yucatán residents 105 MXN. Reset yearly, usually announced in October.
- Opening hours: 08:00–16:00 per INAH. Sources disagree on the entry cut-off: INAH's English page says 15:00, its bulletins say 16:00. Arrive before 15:00 to be safe; staff clear the zone from around 17:00.
- Climbing El Castillo and the other structures has been banned since 2006.
- The equinox serpent shadow on El Castillo appears around 20 March and 22 September, in the late afternoon.
- The entrance moved in 2026. All visitors now enter through the CATVI visitor centre on Highway 180, about 900 m north of El Castillo; the old western Parador Turístico was decommissioned in June 2026. The official sequence now reaches the Sacred Cenote before the pyramid.
- Chichén Itzá is Maya, not Aztec. The Toltecs took the city from the 10th century and built the northern monuments.
